P1.evidence: No setter notes or application read back. Frame was two-part, not four: 'really just want to understand you, where you're at with your fitness journey right now, what you're trying to accomplish' — no 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. Frame agreement was asked for and given: 'if that sounds good' / 'Sure. Sounds good.' Open question ran clean: 'Well, how can I potentially help?'

P2.evidence: Age and weight were volunteered, never asked — 'I've sort of just tipped into 41' and '84... dropped down to 72... now I'm back up to 78'; height never came up. Work was properly explored and the rep landed the physical-labour point: 'So your job is quite physical.' Health conditions and injuries were never asked about at all, even after the prospect volunteered shingles and 'my body sort of starts to tell me... starts to create some pains'. Training week emerged only through questions about the old trainer's programming. Results from current training were asked directly: 'have you plateaued? Have you been continually making gains?' Diet was volunteered ('1800 calories... with all the macros split'), never asked. Sleep and daily energy were never raised.

P3.evidence: Ran the physique scale well — 'scale one to 10... how would you describe your physique right now' → six, wants ten — and checked the modality direction: 'are you looking to build more athleticism, performance, muscle'. Strong bridge to the deeper why: 'what's really behind you wanting to put in the effort to get to like a 10 physique... is there a bigger reason for that?' But never asked for a physical thing he cannot currently do, never asked what moving better would actually do for him, and the impact-on-others question only surfaced late and socially as 'Is your wife into fitness too?'. The reflect-back was attempted as a hypothesis about self-worth — 'I was curious if somehow that is connected to your mindset... your self-worth' — and the prospect agreed, but the rep did not close the loop into kids, marriage, legacy or identity, and did not convert it into the scripted 'so this isn't really about the weight' summary.

P4.evidence: The best-run phase. Fully excavated the previous twelve months of coaching, what the programming was, what results came, and why it ended: 'When did it end with your last trainer?', 'what caused that?', 'was he adapting your programs to your new schedule?'. The prospect named the gap himself when prompted: 'what is it that you feel like you get the most benefit from working with a coach compared to just doing it yourself? Is it like the accountability?' → 'Accountability is definitely one thing... the routine'. Prompting with the answer options is a weaker variant. The rep circled the root cause with 'when you're left to your own devices... is that part of the reason why you fell off?' but let it go when the prospect answered 'potentially, I don't know, to be honest' rather than pressing to a named structural gap.

P5.evidence: The consequence frame was never run in any form. No two-year question, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', no line in the sand. The rep moved from past attempts directly into presenting the programme at 00:35:52 with 'I definitely have some thoughts for you'. Cost of inaction was never made real, which is the most likely reason a warm, high-intent prospect was able to comfortably ask for 48 hours.

P6.evidence: No belief question and no all-in question. The nearest attempt was a gap check after the pillars — 'Is there anything else that you feel like you might want on top of that, or maybe that is missing?' — which tests completeness of the pitch, not commitment. The rep then took 'Cool. So, no questions? It sounds like you feel pretty good about it' as sufficient and let the prospect raise price himself. No verbal yes existed before the number was given, and when hesitation surfaced the rep discounted instead of returning to Phase 5.

P11.evidence: The rep reached the payment conversation — he quoted tiers and structured instalment plans live — so the phase was reachable, but no payment was requested or collected and no payment link was sent. He asked 'What's the best way to get back in touch with you?' and settled for WhatsApp with no date. Steps 2 to 4 (Trevor onboarding call, agreement signature, welcome email and Skool link) are downstream of payment and could not occur once step 1 failed.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger was explicit: 'that's a bit more than what I was expecting' and '$1,400 on top of that's going to be a bit of a stretch'. The rep ran exactly one scripted move — breaking the payment up — and skipped every other one. He never isolated ('finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%'), never used the should-I versus how framing, never asked permission for an honest financial conversation, and took no financial picture at all: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no cards, no available credit, no investments. He then went past the script entirely and cut the total by inventing a three-month $4,000 tier.

Trigger was explicit: 'can I just have a bit of pondering time, like 48 hours'. Not one move ran. No 'do you feel what we've gone through can get you to your goal', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is'. The rep accepted the deferral immediately and moved to logistics.

Trigger was explicit: 'I need to kind of probably discuss it with my wife as well'. The rep asked one clarifying question, 'She wants you to reduce your coaching?', and dropped it. None of the scripted moves ran — no money-aside belief check, no 'what obstacles might come up when you talk to her', no 'is there any reason she would not want you stronger and less in pain', no permission-versus-input reframe, no deposit-with-refund fallback.

Competing-spend objection with no scripted play: the blocker was not capacity to pay in principle but an existing $1,600/month business coach the prospect values and whose value he can articulate. The script has no path for a prospect already funding a different coach at a comparable monthly, and the rep defaulted to lowering the price instead of contesting the priority ordering. This is a script gap, not a rep failure.

notes: Excellent rapport and a genuinely strong Phase 4, then the call fell off a cliff: no consequence frame, no commitment check, and price revealed to a prospect who had never said yes to anything. The single most actionable correction is to run P5 and P6 before the number — and when hesitation came, the rep discounted within ninety seconds rather than returning to Phase 5 as the script requires.
